record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the tenth International conference on fuzzy set theory and applications (FSTA 2010, Liptovsky Jan, Slovakia)
record.original_question: Characterize all triples (S1,S2,T), where S1 and S2 are triangular conorms and T is a triangular norm, such that for every x,y in [0,1] the equality S1(x,y)=S2(T(x,y), T(1-x,y), T(x,1-y)) holds, with S2 applied iteratively according to its associativity. This is a fuzzy-set analogue of decomposing A union B into (A intersection B), (B minus A), and (A minus B).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ be a triangular norm, that is, a binary operation on $[0,1]$ which is commutative, associative, non-decreasing in each argument, and satisfies $T(x,1)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$. Let $S_1,S_2:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ be triangular conorms, i.e., commutative, associative, non-decreasing binary operations on $[0,1]$ satisfying $S_i(x,0)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$. Since $S_2$ is associative, the iterated expression $S_2(a,b,c):=S_2(S_2(a,b),c)$ is well defined.

Characterize all triples $(S_1,S_2,T)$ of triangular conorms $S_1,S_2$ and a triangular norm $T$ such that
$$S_1(x,y)\;=\;S_2\big(T(x,y),\,T(1-x,y),\,T(x,1-y)\big)\qquad\text{for every } x,y\in[0,1].$$

(This identity is the fuzzy-set analogue of the Boolean decomposition $A\cup B = (A\cap B)\cup (B\setminus A)\cup (A\setminus B)$, where $T$ plays the role of intersection and $S_1,S_2$ that of union.)
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in the published collection of open problems from FSTA 2010 (Kybernetika 46(4), 2010, pp. 585–599). A web search did not surface a subsequent paper providing a full characterization of triples $(S_1,S_2,T)$ satisfying this functional equation, so its current status could not be verified.
